newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo to redeem shares at 40 skr premium.
newsitem.headline: Volvo to redeem shares at 40 skr premium.

text.p: Swedish automotive group AB Volvo said on Wednesday that it would redeem a maxium of five percent of its shares at a premium of 40 crowns above the market price.
The share redemption program would cost Volvo about 5.2 billion crowns, the company said in a statement.
Volvo also said its nominating committee decided to propose Hakan Frisinger as the new chairman of Volvo's board, succeeding the late Bert-Olof Svanholm who died on Tuesday.
Volvo has previously said it intends to redeem one in every 20 shares.

Its board will propose at the annual general shareholders' meeting on April 23 that every share in Volvo will give one redemption right and that 20 redemption rights will give a right to redeem one series A or series B share.

The redemption price per share will be determined as the average of the three separate days on which the highest average price for Volvo's series B shares are recorded on the Stockholm Stock Exchange, during the period May 13 to June 6, with the addition of a premium of 40 crowns.

Those registered as shareholders on May 9, 1997, will receive redemption rights. The Volvo share will be quoted excluding the value of this redemption right from and including May 6, the company said.
"Those shareholders not wishing to redeem shares can instead sell their redemption rights and thereby receive the value of Volvo's offer," the company said.
Redemption rights will be listed on the Stockholm bourse and will be traded from May 13 to June 6. American Depository Receipts (ADR) redemption rights will also trade on Nasdaq in the U.S..
The special acceptance period for shareholders wishing to redeem shares will run from May 13 to June 11, Volvo said.
If the redemption is exercised fully, the number of Volvo shares will decline to 441 million from 463.6 million.

"Based on the definitive 1996 financial statements and with full acceptance of the redemption offering, the redemption procedure would result in an increase in profit per share from 26.90 to 27.80," the company said.

Assuming that the redemption price per share will be 225 crowns, shareholders' equity per share at full acceptance will decline to 119.20 crowns from 124.80 crowns and the equity-to-assets ratio would fall to 39.1 percent from 41.4 percent, based on 1996 year-end results, the company said.
The total cost of the redemption of 5.2 billion crowns is calculated on a redemption price of 225 crowns per share.
At 1445 GMT, Volvo's series B shares were trading at 189 crowns on the Stockholm Stock Exchange, up four crowns in the day's trade.
Volvo's proposed new chairman, Hakan Frisinger, was earlier on Wednesday appointed acting chairman until the annual general shareholders' meeting on April 23.
Frisinger, 68, has worked most of his professional life within Volvo. He was president of Volvo Car Corp from 1978 to 1983 and was president of AB Volvo from 1983 to 1987.
The proposal to appoint Frisinger was supported by shareholders representing more than half of the votes and more than one third of the capital, the company said.
